newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Yeltsin may meet in 1997 - White House.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Yeltsin may meet in 1997 - White House.

text.p: The White House on Tuesday confirmed President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin are expected to meet next year, possibly in the first half of 1997 as suggested by the Kremlin.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters Clinton had raised the matter informally in a letter to Yeltsin that reviewed a number of bilateral issues, including arms control and the future of Europe.
"The president added a personal postscript saying that he looks forward to seeing President Yeltsin soon," McCurry said, adding: "I imagine soon as sometime in 1997."
"The Russians have said they hope that will be sometime in the first half of 1997, and I'd say that probably makes a lot of sense," he said, adding that no date or place has been set.
Earlier on Tuesday, a Kremlin spokesman said Yeltsin planned to meet Clinton in the first half of 1997.
The White House said Clinton's letter was delivered by Vice President Al Gore to Russian Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin on Monday in Lisbon, where the two met at a European security summit.

Another White House official suggested that a scheduled February meeting between Gore and Chernomyrdin, who chair a commission on U.S.-Russian relations, might set the stage for a subsequent encounter between Yeltsin and Clinton.
